datasets.verbatim: The DEM data were acquired from the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) of The National Map (TNM), managed by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) [46]... This study utilized the two highest resolution DEMs available in this program: 1-m DEMs acquired in 2018 and 1/9 arc-second DEMs acquired between April 2010 and March 2011.

methods.name: Semi-automatic DEM of Difference (DoD) analysis
methods.summary: The method involves preprocessing multi-temporal DEMs to ensure spatial alignment, calculating a DEM of Difference (DoD) via map algebra to estimate vertical displacement, filtering the DoD using a Level of Detection (LoD) threshold to identify landslide candidates, and using auxiliary vector basemaps and multidirectional Hillshade maps to distinguish landslides from other landscape changes.
methods.source: Behnam Azmoon, Aynaz Biniyaz, and Zhen Liu

availability.author_statement: Data will be available upon request.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is referenced and accessible, and input datasets are publicly available or accessible via standard providers. However, the custom code used for the semi-automatic DEM of Difference analysis is not provided or linked.
